intended_object: For an acyclic orientation O of a multigraph G whose unique source is q, the configuration c(O) = Σ_{v≠q} (indeg_O(v) − 1)·v on V∖{q} (Corry–Perkinson, Definition 4.7, part 2). Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The definition just calls `configOfSource hO`. That function sets chips(v) = 0 when v = q, and chips(v) = indeg_O(v) − 1 otherwise, where indeg_O(v) is the number of directed edges of O that end at v, counted in the multiset of directed edges. In the library, a configuration on q is a divisor with chips(q) = 0 and all values nonnegative. This is the same thing as a configuration on Ṽ = V∖{q} in Corry–Perkinson, so the definition gives exactly c(O) = D(O) restricted to Ṽ.

The hypothesis `acyclicWithUniqueSource` says that O is acyclic and that every source equals q. In an acyclic orientation some source always exists, so q really is the unique source. This matches the book's hypothesis. It also makes the nonnegativity field provable: every v ≠ q has in-degree at least 1.

Chip-firing configurations are not in Mathlib, so there is no counterpart there. The setting (finite multigraphs as given by the library's `CFGraph`) is the standard one for this notion, so the definition is not too narrow.
